title: Design and Implementation of an Automated Illuminating, Culturing, and Sampling System for Microbial Optogenetic Applications
protocol: Solder the Ground, Data, and positive Voltage lines of the digital thermometer to their respective through-holes marked "G D +V."
Clip off one pin from a female 3-pin header.
Trim the remaining two pins with wire clippers so they can fit into the through-holes labelled "R2" without obstructing the microcontroller.
Solder these trimmed pins in place.
Connect the two soldered pins by inserting a 4.7 kΩ resistor in the pin header.
Trim off 1 cm from the pins of five female 3-pin headers.
Solder these trimmed headers to the positions on the PCB marked as "#1," "#2," "#3," "#4," and "C B E."
Trim off 1 cm from the pins of a female 6-pin header.
Trim off 1 cm from the pins of a female 8-pin header.
Solder the 6-pin and 8-pin headers side by side to the column of through-holes labeled K1 through K14.
Connect the heating pad to the circuit board.
Insert the ends of a 100 kΩ resistor in the through-holes labeled K1 and K2 on the PCB.

Insert a metal-oxide-semiconductor field-effect transistor (MOSFET) into the position marked #1 on the PCB, with the label facing towards the K1 through K14 through-holes so that the source pin is closest to the "#" label and the drain pin is furthest from the "#" label.
Cut the ground line of the 5 V DC power supply cable and connect it to J2.
Connect the ground line of the heating pad to J1.
Connect K3 to pin 3 with a 1 kΩ resistor.
Insert the ends of a 100 kΩ resistor in the through-holes labeled K4 and K5 on the PCB.

Insert a MOSFET into the position marked #2 on the PCB, with the label facing towards the K1 through K14 through-holes so that the source pin is closest to the "#" label and the drain pin is furthest from the "#" label.
Cut the ground line of the 12 V DC power supply cable of the slow peristaltic pump.
Connect the peristaltic pump facing end to J3 and the wall wart facing end to J4.
Connect K6 to pin 4 with a 1 kΩ resistor.
Insert the ends of a 100 kΩ resistor in the through-holes labeled K7 and K9 on the PCB.
Insert a MOSFET into the position marked #3 on the PCB, with the label facing towards the K1 through K14 holes.
Cut the ground line of the 12 V DC power supply cable of the fast peristaltic pump.
Connect the peristaltic pump end to J5 and the wall wart end to J6.
Connect K9 to pin 5 with a 1 kΩ resistor.
Solder the 6-pin female pin header into the through-holes on the sides of the PCB.
Solder the 10-pin female pin header into the through-holes on the sides of the PCB.
Solder the two 8-pin female pin headers into the through-holes on the sides of the PCB.
Solder the 100 nF capacitor to its marked position on the PCB.
Solder the negative terminal (shorter lead) of the 10 µF capacitor to the through-hole marked with a negative sign.
Solder the positive terminal of the 10 µF capacitor to its marked position on the PCB.
Solder the LED driver to the 2 by 12 set of through-holes, with the indentation far from the through-holes reserved for the LED matrix.
Solder 2 columns of male pin headers to the through-holes marked for the LED matrix.
Trim the ends of the male pin headers underneath the breadboard such that they will not obstruct the microcontroller.
Connect these 2 columns of male pin headers to two 8-wire strips of female/female jumper wires.
Connect a second set of male pin headers to the other end of the jumper wires.
Insert the LED matrix over the median of the breadboard.
Insert the second set of pin headers into the columns on either side of the matrix.
Clip off one pin from a female 3-pin header.
Trim the remaining two pins with wire clippers to fit into the through-holes labelled "R1".
Solder the trimmed pins.
Insert a 1 kΩ resistor in the soldered pin header.
Stack the PCB on the microcontroller.
Download the Integrated Development Environment (IDE) and custom code for the microcontroller from the materials list links.
Connect the microcontroller to the microscope computer via an A-B USB cable.
Compile and upload the custom code to the microcontroller.
Download Micro-Manager21, 22 and FIJI23.
Copy all ".dll" files, the "mmplugins" directory, and the "mmautofocus" directory from the Micro-Manager download directory into the "Fiji.app" directory.
Copy the "plugins/Micro-Manager" directory from the Micro-Manager download directory into the "Fiji.app/plugins" directory.
Download the "BioreactorController.jar" file into the "Fiji.app/mmplugins" directory.
Open Micro-Manager from FIJI> Plugins> Micro-Manager> Micro-Manager Studio.
Use the Hardware Configuration Wizard to configure the software to control the microscope.
Include the "FreeSerialPort" device in the Wizard with the label of the port to which the A-B USB cable is connected.
Stack three 8 pin IC sockets as building blocks on the breadboard at each corner of the LED matrix such that the culturing vessel can rest on them above the matrix.
Fasten a portion of diffusion paper under the top layer of the sockets, such that the light striking the culturing vessel from the LED matrix is diffuse.
Cut out three 8" by 6" portions of black foam.

Cut out a portion that is the same size as the electronic breadboard (2.3" x 3.5") from the inside of the first two and a portion that is the size of the rectangle made by the IC sockets (0.9" x 1.8") from the inside of the third.
Stack these layers over the LED matrix such that the final layer containing the 0.9" x 1.8" aperture lies even with the top of the IC sockets, and surrounds the LED matrix.
Cut an additional sheet of black foam in half to make a 6" by 24" rectangle.
Roll this into a hollow column of black foam that the culturing vessel can fit into with room for tubes and wires, such that it will thermally and optically insulate the culturing vessel.
Center the hollow column of black foam over the LED matrix.
Mark the boundary of the column on the layer of black foam under it.
Cut out a 3" x 3" portion of black foam.
Attach the photodiode power sensor to the culturing vessel's cap with tape.
Attach the cap to the culturing vessel.
Insert the culturing vessel into the enclosure.
Go to Plugins> Bioreactor Controller in Micro-Manager.
Set the matrix to illuminate at a subset of possible intensities at 30 s intervals.
Record light intensities as displayed on the power meter console connected to the power sensor.
Mark the height corresponding to every 2 mL increment of liquid in the range of 10 mL to 30 mL in the culturing vessel.
Insert 10 mL of sterile deionized water, mark the water level, add 2 mL, mark the water level, and repeat until the 30 mL level is marked.
Cover the markings with clear tape so that they are not easily removed, and dispose of the liquid.
Place the long end of the aluminum port through the silicone gasket, into the culturing vessel.
Screw on the cap.
Cover one short aluminum port outlet with 1/16" ID silicon tubing.
Plug the distal end by inserting a female luer lock and then connecting a male luer lock plug.
Connect two short segments of 1/16" ID silicone tubing with male and female luer locks.
Connect one end to a short aluminum port outlet and plug the distal end with a male luer and female luer lock plug.
Connect two 1/16" ID tubes to the ends of the 1/16" ID peristaltic tubing and connectors.
Connect one end to a short aluminum port and plug the other.
Connect a 1/16" inner diameter silicone tube to the longest aluminum port.
Ensure the tube reaches the media flask.
Attach a 1/8" ID male luer lock to a short segment of 1/16" ID tubing.
Insert this assembly into the rubber stopper on the media flask.
Clamp the connected tubing.
Insert a 1/16" ID tube into the bottom of the flask through the stopper.
Connect another 1/16" ID tube to the first one.
Attach a 3/16" ID tube to the second 1/16" ID tube.
Plug this assembly with a 3/16" ID female luer lock and a male luer lock plug.
Fill the third hole in the stopper with a short segment of 1/16" ID tubing.
Connect two other segments of medium diameter tubing to the filled hole.
Plug the distal end of the tubing assembly.
Insert a male luer lock into a segment of 1/16" ID silicone tubing.
Firmly insert 0.022" ID polytetrafluoroethylene (PTFE) tubing into the setup.
Attach a female luer lock to a 1/16" ID tube separately.
Thread one end along the PTFE tube to connect the locks and the other to a short aluminum port.
Connect the exposed 1/50" ID silicone tube to the 1/50" ID peristaltic tube and connectors.
Connect three segments of 1/50" ID tubing and two segments of 0.022" ID PTFE tubing, alternating them, to the previous connection.
Connect this assembly to the effluent flask via 1/16" ID tubing.
Connect one end of a 1/16" ID silicone tube to the second longest tube of the aluminum port.
Connect the other end to the effluent flask for excess culture overflow management.
Autoclave the culturing assembly at 121 °C and 15 psi for 30 min.
Cure PDMS for 2 hours at 65°C.
Cut PDMS from the mask using a razor blade.
Punch holes at both ends of the channel using a 1.2 mm ID biopsy hole puncher.
Plasma bond PDMS to cover glass.
Tape the long ends of the cover glass to the supporting aluminum frame, ensuring the PDMS channel is centered.
Bake the PDMS again for 2 hours at 65°C.
Prepare appropriate media based on the culturing system requirements.
Attach vacuum filter to a 100 ml bottle.
Remove nipple cover from vacuum filter.
Use sterile tweezers to remove the white plug from the nipple of the vacuum filter.
Connect the 3/16" ID silicone tube to the nipple.
Connect the media flask's other free tube to a vacuum pump.
Ensure that the tube connecting the media flask to the culturing vessel is clamped shut.
Fill the filter with media.
Turn on the vacuum pump and then filter the rest of the media.
Clamp the 1/16" ID silicone tubing connected to the vacuum.
Turn off the vacuum pump.
Remove the luers from the intermediate segment of 1/16" ID tubing connected to the vacuum pump.
Insert the blue end of a sterile syringe air filter into this tube.
Clamp the 3/16" ID silicone tubing.
Disconnect the male luer from it.
Disconnect the plug from the female luer of the culturing vessel's media inlet tube.
Connect these male and female luers to enable media to be pumped into the culturing vessel.
Remove the vacuum filter and cap the 100 mL bottle of media which was attached to the vacuum filter.
Inoculate a single colony of the optogenetic microbe in a test tube with 4 mL of collected media.
Let it grow overnight at 30 °C or the culture's optimal growth temperature with agitation.
Set up the continuous culturing assembly near the microscope with the media flask higher than the culturing vessel and the effluent container lower than the culturing vessel.
Secure rubber stoppers on both the media flask and the effluent container with tape.
Disconnect the ends of the 0.022" ID PTFE tubing from the connecting silicone tube.
Plug the disconnected ends of the 0.022" ID PTFE tubing into the inlet and outlet ports of the microfluidic device.
Connect the white end of the syringe air filter to the aquarium pump to initiate media flow.
Aerate the media by unclamping the air tube between the media flask and culturing vessel when needed.
Tape the heating pad and thermometer to the culturing vessel for temperature control.
Coil the media tubing around the culturing vessel to ensure entering media is at the same temperature as the vessel.
Insert the culturing vessel into the black foam enclosure over the LED matrix.
Ensure that the tubes are not pinched.
In Micro-Manager, go to Plugins> Bioreactor Controller.
Set the "Media pump ratio on" field to 0.1 and the "Sample pump ratio on" field to 0.
Clamp the incoming air tube between the media flask and culturing vessel.
Remove the plug from the inoculation tube (tube 7) and inoculate the culturing vessel with 1 mL of starter culture via a serological pipette.
Clamp and plug the distal end of this tube to ensure that contaminants do not enter the culturing vessel.
Unclamp the incoming air tube.
Cover the enclosure so that no light enters.
Let the culture grow overnight.
In Micro-Manager, go to Plugins> Bioreactor Controller.
Set the "Media pump ratio on" field to 0.5 and the "Sample pump ratio on" field to 0.
Disconnect the overflow tube from the effluent flask (tube 8).
Collect effluent in separate vessels for 1 hr, beginning after the pumps have been on for 15 min.
Calculate the flow rate of media into the culturing vessel from the volume collected in the vessel.
Iterate through this calibration procedure until the difference between the desired flow rate and the measured flow rate is < 0.2 mL/h, where the flow rate is averaged over a 1 h period.

Increase the value of the "sample ratio on" field and calibrate it in a similar manner until roughly 4/5th of the volume leaving the culturing vessel is pumped out by the sampling pump and roughly 1/5th of the volume is leaving through the overflow port.
Let the culture density in the continuous culturing apparatus equilibrate under these conditions overnight.
Fill the Stage Position List in Micro-Manager with a set of non-overlapping positions at which images of cells pumped into the microfluidic channel will be in the focal plane.
Open the "Bioreactor Controller" plugin.
Select the desired LED matrix time course, imaging channels, and other experimental settings from the prompts.
Collect and analyze images.
Ensure that the media in the media flask remains clear while the experiment runs.
Dispose of media, excess cell culture and effluent post-experiment.
Refill the media flask with 200 mL of 20% EtOH mixed with deionized water.
Run the chemostat as it had previously been run during the experiment to wash out cell debris and media.
Disassemble the chemostat fully when the alcohol solution has drained from the media flask.
Wash glassware and tubes with warm water and mild detergent.
Rinse thoroughly with deionized water after washing.
Leave to dry.
